## October Consumer Prices

Consumer prices in South Korea rose 2.8% year-over-year in October, marking the second consecutive month in the upper 2% range. The consumer price index reached 120.73 on a 2020 baseline, according to data released by the National Statistics Office. While agricultural and fisheries prices declined 1.7% with a three-month consecutive drop, processed foods and petroleum products drove inflationary pressure. Oil prices surged 14.9% and processed foods climbed 2.9%, suggesting persistent cost pressures in key consumption categories. The government announced plans to inject 6.4 billion won into price stabilization measures during the kimchi season to ease household burdens.

## Monetary Policy Tensions

The Bank of Korea maintained its benchmark interest rate at 3.00% last month, but growing inflationary momentum is intensifying expectations for additional rate increases. The central bank projects that November inflation will remain in the upper 2% range, signaling continued pricing pressures. Economists worry that expansionary fiscal spending could undermine the Bank of Korea's monetary policy effectiveness, placing additional interest burden on households and businesses. Meanwhile, the Reserve Bank of Australia raised its policy rate to 4.85%, marking the highest level in 18 years and the fifth increase in 2026, driven by persistent price pressures despite concerns about economic slowdown.

## Electric Vehicle Tax Incentives

Parliament's Tax and Finance Subcommittee is expediting legislative efforts to introduce domestic production tax credits for Korean electric vehicles, with a possible full vote expected by early December. This initiative, which has been under legislative consideration since last year, aims to protect domestic automakers against surging Chinese EV imports that now control 83% of the imported electric vehicle market. The Korea Automotive Industry Association warns that without domestic production incentives, approximately 410,000 jobs in the automotive supply chain face serious threats. Industry experts argue that current market conditions demand urgent policy intervention to level the playing field against low-cost Chinese competition.

## CPTPP and Regional Trade Architecture

The Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership comprises 12 member nations and collectively represents approximately 14% of global GDP, creating a major economic bloc across the Pacific. Member nations have achieved a 98.8% tariff elimination rate, covering commodities, digital trade, labor standards, and environmental regulations. For South Korea, CPTPP member nations accounted for 25% of total trade volume last year, making membership consideration particularly significant for accessing this integrated market. Analysts project that participation could generate meaningful GDP growth over a ten-year horizon as tariff barriers diminish.

## Construction Industry Concerns at Nuclear Plants

Construction companies are demanding reform of Korea Hydro and Nuclear Power's special contract provisions, particularly regarding how project delays and cost overruns are allocated. The Ministry of Economy and Finance conducted stakeholder consultations in late October addressing complaints that contractors bear disproportionate financial burdens from design changes and inflation adjustments. The ongoing construction delays at Shin-Kori Units 3 and 4 have resulted in approximately 600 billion won in losses, prompting industry calls for regulatory revisions to align contractual frameworks with current economic realities.

## Stock Market Downturn Amid AI Concerns

The Korean stock market declined sharply on November 3rd, with KOSPI dropping 3.59% as pessimism about artificial intelligence investment returns overshadowed positive signals from declining international oil prices and falling US Treasury yields. KOSDAQ fell 4.0% in tandem, with both indices approaching the 5,600 level. The selloff reflected broader concerns across technology sectors globally, particularly regarding capital adequacy and profitability sustainability in AI-dependent companies. Market participants noted that despite favorable macro indicators, investor skepticism about AI sector valuations proved stronger.

## Samsung BioLogics Contract Success

Samsung BioLogics announced a new 434.3 billion won contract manufacturing agreement with a global pharmaceutical company through December 2031, marking the ninth contract disclosed this year and bringing cumulative order backlog to 22.3 billion dollars since its founding. The company also increased an existing US pharmaceutical supply agreement by 62.8 billion won, demonstrating consistent momentum in the contract development and manufacturing organization sector. Samsung BioLogics continues executing a three-pronged expansion strategy encompassing production capacity increases, business diversification into antibody-drug conjugates and peptide therapeutics, and geographic expansion including its August opening of a European operations office in the Netherlands.

## Nuclear and Energy Cooperation with Turkey

President Lee Myung-bak met with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, agreeing to expand bilateral cooperation in nuclear energy, defense industry, and resource sectors. The Korea Export-Import Bank and Turkey's Nuclear Energy Authority signed a memorandum of understanding on nuclear project financing, establishing strategic information-sharing mechanisms and financial support frameworks for Korean company participation. The nations also concluded agreements on artificial intelligence, biotechnology, and other advanced technology sectors, signaling broadened economic partnership beyond traditional energy collaboration.

## Real Estate Market Uncertainty

Despite government expectations for housing price stabilization by year-end, only 10 to 20 percent of real estate professionals and brokers surveyed expect Seoul apartment prices to stabilize within the next year. Market sentiment reveals significant divergence from official government projections, with particular weakness in Gangnam district where reconstruction apartment prices have declined notably. Rental market instability is expected to persist alongside sales market uncertainty. Gyeonggi Province housing prices have risen notably, driven by semiconductor and advanced industrial cluster developments, with Seongnam posting 18.66 points of appreciation and Gwangmyeong recording 18.52 points over the past year.

## US Midterm Election Economic Impact

American voters express substantial dissatisfaction with inflation and cost-of-living pressures, with 70% disapproving of the Trump administration's inflation response according to pre-election polling. Energy price increases from Iran-related tensions and tariff policy impacts have elevated economic issues as central election concerns. Meanwhile, Wall Street leaders assert that AI infrastructure investment demands remain robust, with Morgan Stanley projecting cumulative investment reaching 15 trillion dollars over the next decade as major hyperscaler companies could deploy 800 billion to 1 trillion dollars annually for seven to twelve years.

## For Investors and Households

The current economic backdrop presents mixed signals for investors and consumers. Persistent inflation at 2.8% suggests the Bank of Korea must carefully calibrate rate policy to prevent undermining economic growth while maintaining price stability. Stock market volatility driven by AI sector concerns underscores the importance of portfolio diversification beyond technology-dependent companies. For households, inflationary pressures on energy and food costs persist despite some agricultural price relief, necessitating continued attention to budget management. The shift toward domestic EV production incentives and expanded international trade partnerships through agreements like CPTPP offers longer-term growth opportunities, while real estate market uncertainty warrants cautious approach to major property investments. Global trade dynamics, particularly regarding US tariff policies and Chinese EV competition, will substantially influence Korean export-dependent sectors throughout the coming quarters.
headline: October Inflation Holds at 2.8% as Korea Weighs Rate Decision
